thread:
oncall-bot: P0: Dedicated pool sustained high utilization — dedicated-prod-us-central-1 autoscaler not provisioning fast enough. Paging oncall.
Priya: ack. seeing sharp rise in model queue depth across pool; GPU util ~92% for last 3m. 95th latency for chat.generate jumped from ~200ms -> 1.1s. error spikes include 429 + 504.
Nina: grabbing per-org breakdown. Looks like one org fired a large overnight job (org noisy-ops). Estimated extra qps ~850 on top of baseline.
Jared: any recent config changes to autoscaler or node templates? I don't see infra deploys in the last hour.
Priya: none. I'm checking autoscaler controller logs.
infra-bot: Alert — cloud API rate-limit observed when requesting VMs: 429 (Request throttled). Recent 6/10 attempts failed.
Priya: that explains provisioning lag. Immediate mitigations: 1) enable spillover routing to fallback pool (dedicated-prod-us-west-2) for non-SLA traffic 2) temporarily bump pool burst_capacity and cooldown 3) apply per-org emergency throttle for noisy-ops 4) disable batched analytics exports.
Jared: I can flip spillover routing for public-scope routes. Priya — which routes should we exclude? We must not spill critical enterprise paid routes.
Priya: spillover only for non-enterprise flag routes: set route.selector != enterprise. That should move best-effort traffic.
Jared: running routing change:
```
routingctl set-spillover --src-pool dedicated-prod-us-central-1 --dst-pool dedicated-prod-us-west-2 --selector "!enterprise" --ttl 20m --reason "live mitigation autoscaler lag"
```
infra-bot: Spillover rule active. Estimated offload ~40% of best-effort qps.
Priya: applying burst increase to pool:
```
infractl pools update --pool dedicated-prod-us-central-1 --burst-multiplier 1.8 --cooldown 120s --reason "temporary burst during provisioning lag"
```
infra-bot: pool update acknowledged.
Nina: also going to escalate a temporary org throttle for noisy-ops: set rps 30, burst 60 for 20m.
```
api-gateway throttle --org noisy-ops --rps 30 --burst 60 --duration 20m --reason "mitigate noisy job"
```
infra-bot: org throttle applied.
Support-Escalation: I've DM'd noisy-ops and enterprise contacts. noisy-ops acknowledged and paused their job.
Priya: disabling analytics export that fans out to model calls:
```
feature-flag disable analytics.exports --env dedicated-prod-us-central-1 --reason "reduce model call fanout"
```
infra-bot: analytics.exports disabled.
Priya: monitoring: within 90s queue depth down ~35%, 95th latency down to ~600ms. error rate trending down but still elevated.
Jared: question — do we need to manually reserve instances while provider quota is being reviewed? We have spare reserved capacity option. I can provision 4 reserved nodes in us-central-1.
Priya: yes, do a manual reserve for 4 nodes for 45m. Command:
```
infractl pools reserve --pool dedicated-prod-us-central-1 --count 4 --ttl 45m --reason "manual reserve while cloud quota recovers"
```
infra-bot: reserve request issued.
Nina: autoscaler logs show cloud provider returning 429 for create requests; I've opened ticket CP-99921 and linked provider support. They estimate 10-15m to lift throttling.
Priya: handoff soon — I'll need to step away for an incident call in ~8m. Jared, can you take lead? Handoff notes: spillover rule active, burst_multiplier 1.8, org noisy-ops throttled to 30rps/60burst for 20m, analytics exports disabled, 4-node reserve requested.
Jared: taking lead. I'll keep monitoring routing metrics and provider ticket. Plan to revert in controlled order: 1) remove reserve after 30m stable 2) restore analytics 3) remove org throttle 4) disable spillover and revert burst_multiplier.
oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. New oncall: Jared.
infra-bot: snapshot: queue depth returning to baseline, 95th latency ~320ms, error rate 0.6%.
Jared: leaving a short customer-impact note: impacted window ~10m, primary symptom elevated latency and 429 for best-effort workloads; some enterprise retries observed but no data loss. Root cause: cloud provider API throttling slowed autoscaler, amplified by a large noisy org workload.
Nina: follow-ups: 1) add provider API 429 alerting tied to autoscaler controller 2) add pre-warmed standby nodes for critical pools during business hours 3) add per-org heavy-job detection and early throttling runbook steps.
Jared: I'll open tickets and tag infra/reliability. Support — please confirm any customers still seeing issues.
Support-Escalation: noisy-ops and a couple of beta customers confirmed reduced errors; noisy-ops will schedule heavy job for off-peak.
Jared: I'll keep the reserve for 35m then start rollback if metrics stable for 20m. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Priya: back from call, thanks for taking lead.
infra-bot: change-log: spillover_rule=active 00:00:22, burst_multiplier=1.8 00:00:45, org-throttle noisy-ops 00:01:10, analytics.exports disabled 00:01:35, reserve=4 nodes requested 00:03:00.
Jared: final check at 1963510120: autoscaler recovered and accepted new nodes; metrics stable. Scheduling controlled rollback to start in 10m. Incident will be documented in postmortem.
